predecessors.name: Anglo-Saxon England (early settlement)
predecessors.text: Mercia's first Cliopatria shape: 104 of its 105 cells lie in the anglo-saxon-england dossier's successor land for Mercia

successors.name: Kingdom of Wessex
successors.text: Mercia as it stood in 918 (the western half without Oxford, plus Derby and Leicester), taken by Edward the Elder

ledger.x: 527: the kingdom of Mercia is established under Icel.
617: Cliopatria's shape grows about 3.5 thousand km2 to the north-west (bounding box 2.8-2.0 W, 52.9-53.4 N).
628: Penda takes the Hwicce country after Cirencester: 'following the Battle of Cirencester of 628, when Penda incorporated the formerly West Saxon territories of Hwicce'.
628: Cliopatria's shape adds a further 7 thousand km2 across the Midlands (2.9-0.8 W, 51.7-53.5 N) beyond the Hwicce.
656: Oswiu of Northumbria takes Mercia after Penda's fall at the Winwaed (15 November 655, Wulfhere page).
658: Mercia throws off Northumbrian rule under Wulfhere.
661: Wulfhere takes the Isle of Wight.
661: Wulfhere takes the Meon valley with the Isle of Wight.
661: Wulfhere gives the Isle of Wight and the Meon valley to Æthelwealh of Sussex.
664: the East Saxon kings rule under Wulfhere.
674: Wulfhere loses Lindsey to Northumbria and the fight for it begins.
679: Æthelred beats Ecgfrith at the Trent.
679: Æthelred takes Lindsey for Mercia: he 'defeated Northumbria in the Battle of the Trent in 679', settling 'the long-disputed control of the former kingdom of Lindsey'.
688: Oswine takes the Kentish throne with Mercian backing.

c. 691: Wihtred succeeds and Oswine's Mercian-backed kingship ends. 'The overlap in date ranges gives April to July 691 as the likely date of his accession.' The page does not say that Mercian overlordship stopped; the end is a bridge, as in the Kent dossier (confidence 1).
705: the Welsh border strip around Wroxeter passes to Mercia in Cliopatria's shape.
705: the Dee plain passes to Mercia in Cliopatria's shape.
705: the Archenfield cell passes to Mercia in Cliopatria's shape.
726: Æthelbald makes Mercia the leading power south of the Humber, Wessex included.
752: Wessex throws off Mercian hegemony.
757: the West Saxons recover the border strip on the Thames.
764: Offa's influence in Kent is first attested.
771: Offa conquers Sussex.
776: Kent slips out of Mercian authority at Otford.
779: Offa wins the Thames-valley border strip back at Bensington: 'Offa won an important victory over Cynewulf at the Battle of Bensington (in Oxfordshire) in 779.'
785: Offa re-establishes his authority over Kent.
786: Offa and Wessex.
794: Offa has the East Anglian king executed and rules East Anglia.
796: Offa dies and Kent rebels.
796: East Anglia revives after Offa's death.
798: Coenwulf reconquers Kent.

c. 799: Coenwulf suppresses Eadwald and East Anglia is a Mercian client again. Infobox 'Client state of Mercia (794-796; c. 799-825)'; the page dates the suppression no closer. The Coenwulf page says only that 'In East Anglia, King Eadwald minted coins at about this time, implying that he was no longer subject to…
802: Wessex leaves Mercian overlordship.
806: three cells of the Thames west of London pass from Wessex to Mercia in Cliopatria's shapes.
825: Ellandun ends the Mercian Supremacy.
825: Essex leaves Mercian overlordship.
825: East Anglia leaves Mercian overlordship.
825: Sussex goes to Wessex.
829: Ecgberht of Wessex conquers Mercia.
830: Wiglaf restores Mercia.
840: Cliopatria adds the Essex-London area (4.3 thousand km2, 0.6 W-0.7 E, 51.5-51.9 N) to Mercia.
852: Mercia and Wessex subject North Wales.
866: Cliopatria takes about 4.3 thousand km2 of north Midlands and Lindsey (0.9 W-0.1 E, 52.6-53.5 N) from Mercia in 866, the year its Viking settlements shape first touches Mercia.
868: the Danes occupy Nottingham.
874: the Danes drive Burgred out and set up Ceolwulf II.
875: London passes to Alfred: 'in about 875, Alfred was the sole recognised ruler in London'.
877: the Danes take the eastern half of Mercia.
879: the last king ends and Mercia becomes a client of Wessex.
879: Mercia becomes a client state of Wessex.
881: North Wales shakes off Mercia.
883: Æthelred rules Mercia as Lord of the Mercians under Wessex.
886: Alfred takes London from the Danes and gives it to Æthelred.
911: Æthelred dies and his widow Æthelflæd rules Mercia as Lady of the Mercians: 'Æthelred died in 911 and Æthelflæd then ruled Mercia as Lady of the Mercians.'
911: Edward the Elder takes London and Oxford: 'When Æthelred died, Edward took control of the Mercian towns of London and Oxford.'
917: Æthelflæd takes Derby from the Danes: 'Æthelflæd, Lady of the Mercians, took the borough of Derby.'
918: Leicester submits to Æthelflæd.

December 918: Edward the Elder ends Mercia's client status by taking it into his own hands. Æthelflæd died at Tamworth on 12 June 918; 'in early December 918 Edward deposed her [her daughter Ælfwynn] and took Mercia under his control.'
918: Edward the Elder ends Mercia. Æthelflæd died at Tamworth on 12 June 918; 'in early December 918 Edward deposed her [her daughter Ælfwynn] and took Mercia under his control.'

wars.name: Penda's wars with Northumbria
wars.outcome: Penda and Cadwallon of Gwynedd defeated and killed Edwin in 633; Maserfield followed in 642; Penda lost battle and life at the Winwaed in 655, Oswiu took direct control of Mercia in 656 and a revolt freed it in 658.

wars.name: Wulfhere's campaigns in the south
wars.outcome: Wulfhere harried Ashdown and raided the Isle of Wight in 661, then gave the island and the Meon valley to Æthelwealh of the South Saxons.

wars.name: Battle of the Trent
wars.outcome: Ecgfrith of Northumbria forced Wulfhere to surrender Lindsey (674); Æthelred of Mercia won the Trent in 679 and Lindsey became a client of Mercia.

wars.name: Offa's wars with Wessex
wars.outcome: Cynewulf recovered border land from 757; Offa won at Bensington in 779 and may have placed Beorhtric on the throne in 786.

wars.name: Offa's campaigns in Kent and Sussex
wars.outcome: Mercian influence in Kent from 764, the fight at Otford in 776 (outcome unrecorded), Hastings defeated in 771, Offa's authority in Kent clear in charters of 785-89.

wars.name: Offa's Welsh campaigns
wars.outcome: Fights at Hereford (760) and campaigns in 778, 784 and 796; Offa's Dyke marks the frontier.

wars.name: Battle of Ellandun
wars.outcome: Ecgberht beat Beornwulf in 825; Kent, Essex, Surrey and Sussex submitted and East Anglia sought his protection.

wars.name: Mercian and West Saxon conquest of North Wales
wars.outcome: Burgred and Æthelwulf 'subjugated North Wales' in 852; Rhodri Mawr died fighting the English in 878 and his sons beat the Mercians at the Conwy in 881.

wars.name: Danish invasions of Mercia
wars.outcome: Nottingham occupied in 868, Burgred driven out in 874, Ceolwulf II installed, the eastern part seized in 877 and joined to the Danelaw; Ceolwulf kept the western half.

wars.name: Æthelflæd's wars with the Danes
wars.outcome: The Danish army was destroyed at Tettenhall (910); Derby fell in 917 and Leicester submitted in 918. Æthelflæd died on 12 June 918.

certainty.note: No treaty or survey line is on any page opened; the frontier with the Welsh kingdoms and the Hwicce, Lindsey and Essex edges are approximate.

Offa's Dyke, 'created as the boundary between Mercia and the Welsh kingdoms' and 'probably built in his reign', is the one built frontier, but it is not dated and no source gives its line; the Danelaw frontier fixed 'Between 886 and 890'…
